Subject: Next steps: deployment compatibility + migration checklist

Hi Alex — thanks for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Recap: you described a production recommender that needs sub-100ms tail latency for small text inputs, currently serving from an internal GPU cluster, and a requirement to keep customer vectors under your control for compliance. You also mentioned wanting to explore moving off your legacy internal endpoint to reduce ops overhead.

Questions to help qualify:
- Can you confirm whether your current stack uses a custom auth layer in front of the GPU cluster (JWT/OAuth proxy) or if calls are direct to an internal HTTP API?
- Do you have hard retention or audit-log requirements beyond SOC2 (e.g., region-specific data residency for EU customers)?
- Expected sustained QPS and peak QPS for inference (tokens/sec or requests/sec) and typical sequence length?
- Any blockers for a Private VPC (network approvals, on-prem air-gap, or hardware procurement timelines)?

Initial thoughts (high level):
- If you require strict vector custody + private networking and can tolerate some ops overhead, Private VPC or on-prem is likely the best fit.
- If the ops team wants us to handle patching/scale and the data residency can be addressed via contractual controls, Dedicated capacity gives predictable throughput and quick time-to-production.
- Hosted API is fastest but may not satisfy your vector custody ask without additional controls.

Next steps I propose: we run a short compatibility gap assessment (lightweight technical intake) and then pick one of three mutual action plans (Pilot on Hosted with token-level routing, Pilot on Dedicated using a dedicated pool, or PoC for Private VPC). I attached a one-page checklist to guide the intake.

Can you reply with answers to the four bullets above and share a rough QPS estimate by EOD tomorrow? I’ll pull Karthik and Ben into a short technical scoping session after we get that.

Thanks,
Priyom
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Radev <alex@retailai.com>

Date: 2026-06-22T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Next steps: deployment compatibility + migration checklist

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the recap. Answers below:

- Auth: we have an OAuth2 proxy in front of the cluster; tokens are validated by our API gateway. We do not currently support mutual TLS.
- Compliance: SOC2 is baseline; additionally, we must keep EU customer embeddings stored in EU for at-rest residency. We already tag customer data by region in our DB.
- Load: steady-state ~120 reqs/sec (average inference payload ~350 tokens), peaks up to ~750 reqs/sec during promos. Typical latency requirement is P95 < 150ms, but lower is preferred.
- Private VPC blockers: legal is open to it, but our infra team would prefer Redwood-managed Dedicated if it avoids a long procurement and rack/cabinet coordination. On-prem is a hard no for now.

We are interested in a route that minimizes ops overhead but meets residency. If Dedicated can be provisioned in an EU region for EU customers and US for US customers, that might be the short path. Happy to join a scoping session tomorrow afternoon.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
RetailAI

Thanks — good data from Alex. A few technical notes and a proposed pilot recommendation:

Notes:
- OAuth2 proxy is fine; we can front Redwood Dedicated or Private VPC with token verification. mTLS is optional but adds an extra ops step for RetailAI.
- EU data residency: we can provision Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 and route EU traffic there. That meets at-rest location and simplifies vector custody since data never leaves the EU pool.
- Latency: P95 150ms at 750 rps peak is tough but achievable if we:
  - use model variants with lower memory footprint (8-bit/quantized) for bulk traffic,
  - enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, and
  - reserve a Dedicated pool sized for burst headroom (we can run perf sims in a week).

Recommendation: start with a two-phased pilot:
1) Dedicated pilot scoped by region (US + EU) for 6 weeks to validate latency and routing. This minimizes procurement friction per Alex and keeps vectors under control.
2) If Dedicated pilot shows unacceptable unit cost or latency variance, transition to Private VPC PoC for the EU subset.

Technical asks for the intake session (we should collect these before the scoping call):
- current request signing flow (sample JWT claims),
- representative production traffic trace (1 hour sample at peak),
- a staging model binary or Hugging Face model name if you self-host today,
- firewall/egress rules for network kickoff.

I can run the perf sim if Alex shares a 1-hour trace. Ben — can you prepare a high-level pricing sketch for a 6-week Dedicated pilot (US+EU) so legal/procurement can budget?

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
